A content delivery network, or CDN, is a system that helps websites load quickly no matter where a visitor is located. Normally, a website's files live on a single computer called the origin server — the original home of all the images, videos, and text that make up a site. If everyone on the planet had to fetch those files from one distant computer, loading a page could feel slow, especially for people far away. A CDN solves this by copying those files onto many smaller computers scattered around the world, called edge locations, because they sit at the "edge" of the network, close to where people actually are. Think of it like a chain of bakeries that all sell the same bread recipe, so customers can grab a fresh loaf from the shop nearest them instead of traveling to one central bakery in another country. When someone visits a website, their device is directed to the nearest edge location instead of the far-off origin server. If that nearby location already has a stored copy of the requested file, this is called a cache hit, and the file is delivered almost instantly. If not, the edge location fetches it once from the origin server, saves a copy for next time, and passes it along. This system reduces waiting time, eases pressure on the original computer, and keeps things running smoothly even when many people request the same content at once. In short, a CDN shortens the distance information has to travel.

| Term | Plain meaning | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Origin server | The original computer where a website's files are stored | It is the ultimate source of truth, used when no nearby copy exists |
| Edge location | A smaller, nearby computer holding copies of website files | It sits close to visitors, cutting down travel distance and wait time |
| Cache hit | When a nearby edge location already has the requested file ready | It means near-instant delivery without bothering the origin server |
| Latency | The delay between requesting a file and receiving it | Lower latency means pages feel faster and smoother to use |
